| D1 | Workspace initialization uses `workspace[tile_size]` as a live scalar-array declarator target. It is allocation/declarator syntax, not an rvalue access, and `VarInit.var` must remain an exact `Var`. Rejected. |
| W1 | Untiled workspace copy reads `workspace[loop_var]` as a fresh `NO_TYPE` value. Supported dense workspaces use `memcpy` or the already structured tiled route. Rejected. |
| C1/C2 | The all-COO pre-scan reads `crd[_p]` and `crd[_p - 1]` through borrowed input pointers. Its production caller discards this pre-scan tree. Rejected. |
| G1/G2 | The discarded all-COO group loop reads `_group_starts[_g]` and `_group_starts[_g + 1]` as promoted `INT64` values from an owned `std::vector<int>`. These reads also participate in the legacy bracket-to-`.at(...)` rewrite. Rejected. |
| I1/I2 | Coordinate `ModeIterator` alternatives read `tensorN_pos[0]` and `[1]` as `INT` iterator bounds. Production root lowering emits literal zero and derives `.size(0)`, so these alternatives do not reach generated LLIR. Rejected. |
| K1-K6 | Six live `.data_ptr<T>()` leaves have exact borrowed pointer types and are coupled to Torch-owned input/result/intermediate tensors. A templated member-call representation is required. Retained as a separate future call seam. |
| K7/K8 | Two live schedule-storage `.data()` leaves borrow exact pointers from owned vectors. They require the same deferred member/call-on-expression hierarchy. Retained as a separate future call seam. |
| B1-B3 | Three `.storage` members are Torch result-ABI lvalues or a dormant compatibility read. They require coordinated member assignment/ABI work. Retained as a separate future member seam. |
| N3/T1 | The result `mode_indices` initializer and discarded all-COO ternary require, respectively, coordinated result-ABI initializer support and a conditional expression representation. Retained as independent future seams. |

The complete 40-constructor `RawStmt` inventory was then classified by
producer, consumer, type, ownership, production reachability, exact source
spelling, and compatibility-rewrite interaction:

| ID | Producer and exact payload family | Consumer, ownership/reachability, rewrite interaction, and decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | `cin_lowerer.py`: `std::vector<int> ResultN_pos((size_t)ResultParent_size + 1, 0)` | Live owning fixed-position vector. Direct initialization/allocation has no existing byte-exact statement representation; rejected. |
| C2 | Torch coordinate allocation plus `int* = tensor.data_ptr<int>()` | Live Torch-owned coordinate storage and borrowed pointer. Compound allocation and templated member call; rejected as Torch ABI/allocation work. |
| C3 | `int64_t size = actual_size` | Live dense-workspace extent alias; its uses remain coupled to raw zero-fill/copy/pool statements. Individually expressible but not a complete family; rejected. |
| C4 | `ctype* __restrict__ wksp = pool_owner.get() + thread offset` | Live borrowed per-worker slice. Member call, pointer arithmetic, casts, and pool ownership are coupled; rejected. |
| C5 | `memset(wksp, 0, size * sizeof(ctype))` | Live workspace mutation. This is the explicitly deferred parallel zero-fill seam; rejected. |
| C6 | `memcpy(&Result_values[row * stride], wksp, size * sizeof(ctype))` | Live workspace-to-result copy exposed to raw compatibility replacement. Requires address-of and coordinated copy representation; rejected. |
| C7 | `_dynamic_reserve = std::min<int64_t>(checked_product(...), 2048)` | Live `INT64` reserve-policy value. Nested templated/qualified calls and dynamic allocation policy are coupled; rejected. |
| C8-C10 | `validate_jit_result_shape(...)`, `validate_jit_tensor(...)`, and `validate_jit_extra_tensor(...)` | Live side-effecting result/input/extra-tensor validation. One TorchCppABI validation family; rejected. |
| C11 | `int64_t _known_nnz = Input_values.size(0)` | Live cardinality query borrowing an input Torch tensor. Requires member-call-on-expression support; rejected. |
| C12 | `int _nnz = Sparse_pos[outer_bound]` | Live adaptive work-stealing state and visible to sparse-position discovery. Coupled to rendered scheduling policy C13; rejected as unrelated optimization work. |
| C13 | `_chunk = std::max(16, std::min(256, _nnz / (...)))` | Live adaptive scheduling state consumed by atomic-loop metadata/codegen. Same excluded optimization family as C12; rejected. |
| C14 | `std::atomic<int> _next_row{0}` | Constructed on the adaptive branch but retained only in unread `_atomic_counter_decl`; codegen emits its own declaration. Non-emitting; rejected rather than beginning DCE. |
| C15 | `int wksp_thread_count = thread_expr` | Live before-parallel scalar coupled to raw thread-policy text and pool allocation C16; rejected. |
| C16 | `auto wksp_pool_owner = scorch_make_aligned_buffer<T>(checked_size_product(...))` | Live RAII workspace owner. Generalized allocation and templated-call family; rejected. |
| C17 | `output_array.resize(outer_end)` | Constructed by the all-COO transform, but its scalar-accumulation production caller discards the preallocation statements. Non-emitting production route plus member-call hierarchy; rejected. |
| W1 | `auto wksp = wksp_pool[(size_t)omp_get_thread_num()].make_view()` | Live borrowed worker view for DS/DSS. Requires call-on-structured-subscript/member hierarchy; rejected. |
| W2/W4 | `wksp.clear()` in count/fill bodies | Live mutations of the borrowed view. Moving the dotted spelling into `FunctionCallStmt.name` would only relocate opacity; rejected as one member-call family. |
| W3 | `int64_t _baseN = _offsetN[loop_var]` | Live per-level fill base copied from an owned `std::vector<int64_t>`; all consumers are typed. Existing nodes can represent it, but `_offset` allocation/prefix generation and its raw offset-family consumers remain opaque. Retained as the runner-up rather than leaving a mixed raw/structured offset family. |
| W5 | Thread-count, `vector<linked_list_workspace>`, reserve loop, and `emplace_back` compound statement | Live owner of DS/DSS per-worker sparse workspaces. Compound allocation/loop/member-call family; rejected. |
| W6 | `std::vector<int> _countN((size_t)bound, 0)` | Live owned count vector. Direct-initialization/allocation seam; rejected. |
| W7 | `std::vector<int64_t> _offsetN((size_t)bound + 1)` | Live owned offset vector. Same allocation/declarator seam; rejected. |
| W8 | Compact prefix loop assigning `_offset[i + 1] = _offset[i] + _count[i]` | Live mutation of W7 from W6. It remains a generic raw traversal leaf but is not matched by the `_pos[...]` position scanners. Existing `ForLoop` would change exact layout/spelling; rejected. |
| W9 | `int64_t _totalN = _offsetN[bound]` | Live level cardinality, but every consumer is in Torch allocation statements W10/W12-W14. Even a combined W3+W9 slice would leave W6-W8 and all `_totalN` allocation consumers opaque, so it is not a complete offset/cardinality family. Rejected. |
| W10 | First-position Torch allocation plus `int* data_ptr` | Live Torch-owned storage and borrowed pointer. Compound allocation/member-call seam; rejected. |
| W11 | Compact loop copying `_offset` to the first position tensor | Live initialization of W10. Coupled to its allocation and would change source layout if expanded structurally; rejected. |
| W12 | Coordinate Torch allocation plus `int* data_ptr` | Live once per compressed level. Torch allocation/member-call seam; rejected. |
| W13 | Deeper position allocation plus `int* data_ptr` | Live for multi-compressed-level results such as DSS. Same Torch seam; rejected. |
| W14 | Value Torch allocation plus typed `data_ptr<T>()` | Live Torch-owned values and borrowed pointer. Same Torch seam; rejected. |
| W15 | Compound `Tensor result`, storage assignments, and `return` | Live final result assembly. TorchCppABI/member-assignment extraction; rejected. |
| D1 | `const T* __restrict__ ptr = &value_array[base * stride]` | Live borrowed dense pointer. Exact raw grammar is consumed by sparse-prefetch compatibility code; arbitrary `const T*` and address-of are not represented. Rejected. |
| R1 | `llir_traversal.py` `RawStmt(code=node.code, add_semicolon=node.add_semicolon)` | Common detached clone, not a semantic producer. Must remain while any raw family exists; this accounts for 40 constructors versus 39 producers. |
| L1 | `float _inv_N = rendered_invariant` | Live scalar-accumulator SDDMM loop-invariant materialization, including DS-mask and all-COO paths. Owns the local and is always paired with L2. Selected as typed `VarInit`. |
| L2 | `accumulator *= _inv_N` | Live post-loop mutation of the original typed scalar/member target and always paired with L1. Selected as typed `Assign(MUL_ASSIGN)`. |
| S1 | Packed-storage prefetch conditional | Live only when relayout redirects prefetch. Conditional/address-of/nested-subscript optimization representation is absent; rejected. |
| S2 | `std::vector<T> tiled_Result_storage((size_t)prefix * (size_t)tile)` | Live owning schedule storage with deferred `.data()` consumer. Generalized allocation/direct-init seam; rejected. |
| S3 | `std::vector<T> packed_Operand_storage((size_t)rows * (size_t)tile)` | Live owning relayout storage with deferred `.data()` consumer. Same allocation seam; rejected. |
| P1 | Future-position `__builtin_prefetch(&value[coord[next] * stride], 0, 1)` conditional | Live sparse/dense optimization, rewritten or replaced by later compatibility/schedule work. Address-of/conditional/prefetch representation is absent; rejected. |

The first audit conservatively rejected L1/L2 because its private renderer had
a broad fallback. Reinspection proved that every live production factor is
already an LLIR expression accepted by common codegen; this is the complete
live production factor set, not every expression class admitted elsewhere in
LLIR. Removing the duplicate renderer therefore narrows the compiler
rather than creating a parser or hierarchy. Live production spelling remains
byte-for-byte identical. Two synthetic-only expectations intentionally become
canonical common-codegen spelling: redundant product parentheses collapse to
`inv_a * inv_b * inv_c`, and a synthetic `FunctionCall` now emits `scale(x)`
instead of its dataclass representation. Neither spelling appears in the
production capture grid.

L1/L2 are the smallest complete live family: one producer site always creates
the declaration/post pair, both are owned by the loop-invariant-factor pass,
and existing `VarInit`, `Assign`, `Var`, `ArrayAccess`, and common codegen cover
the whole boundary. Selecting only W3 would structure one read while leaving
its offset allocation, prefix mutation, totals, and compatibility-visible
consumers opaque. The selected pair requires no ABI change, generalized
member/call or allocation hierarchy, parser, zero-fill extraction, DCE, or
unrelated optimization.

#### Representation, traversal, ownership, and compatibility audit

The generated pair is now:

```python
llir.VarInit(
    var=llir.Var(name=invariant_name, type=llir.DataType.FLOAT32),
    value=invariant_expression,
)
llir.Assign(
    var=fresh_exact_accumulator_var,
    value=llir.Var(name=invariant_name, type=llir.DataType.FLOAT32),
    op=llir.AssignOp.MUL_ASSIGN,
)
```

The declaration, declaration child, accumulator target, and invariant
reference are independently owned. The accumulator copy preserves the exact
name, type, and pointer/restrict flags of the matched target together with the
required scalar-target `tensor_access=None` invariant.
Structural equality is preserved across independent compilations; `VarInit`
hashing remains defined by its `Var`, while mutable `Assign` remains
intentionally unhashable. No caller-owned CIN/LLIR object or exact
`CompileOptions` object is mutated or replaced.

`ArrayAccess` remains the existing frozen structural expression with exact
LLIR expression children and exact optional `TensorAccessMetadata`. Equality
and hashing include array/index structure but intentionally exclude provenance
metadata. Common traversal visits array then index in deterministic preorder,
identity rewriting creates detached nodes and children on every run, and
replacement rewriting owns the replacement. Common codegen preserves postfix
and arithmetic precedence. Exact-dispatch traversal/codegen reject unknown
children and `ArrayAccess` subclasses. The live `_inv_17` initializer reuses
the already structured `Mask_val[pMask0]` expression, including exact
`PTR_FLOAT32`/`INT` children and input-read metadata.

The factor pass validates the complete emitted pair at its own boundary. It
requires exact `VarInit`/`Assign` nodes, exact scalar `Var` children, `_inv_N`
`FLOAT32` declaration/reference agreement, default declaration fields, and an
uncast `MUL_ASSIGN`. The declaration value must be the selected invariant
owned by the materialization, and the post target must exactly match the
selected body assignment's name, type, and pointer/restrict flags. It then
walks both nodes with the common validator, so forged fields, values, targets,
subclasses, and unknown children fail before a run record or later work can be
published.

The old raw declaration was intentionally invisible to the pass's legacy
substring definition scan. The final recognizer requires position-matched
`_inv_N` declarations, the wrapped exact loop, reverse-ordered matching post
assignments, and a selected loop-body accumulator target. It handles nested
wrappers created by repeated rewriting while keeping ordinary declaration plus
unrelated-later-multiply lookalikes visible. This preserves nested-loop
classification and legacy `_inv_N` collision behavior without hiding ordinary
non-wrapper `VarInit` definitions. Dense-pointer, single-iteration, sparse-prefetch,
and dynamic-vector passes traverse the new nodes normally. Dynamic-vector
deduplication considers only adjacent equal indexed `Assign(ASSIGN)` writes to
declared dynamic coordinate vectors, so it cannot consume a scalar
`MUL_ASSIGN`; equal repeated materializations remain distinct and detached.
The ten generic string rewrites have no selected bracket/member spelling to
rewrite.

On malformed live all-COO output, the exact prior managed records for sparse
prefetch, dense-pointer hoisting, and single-iteration elimination remain;
the owning factor record is absent. Result assembly, dynamic-vector rewriting,
function construction, schedule lowering, codegen, build/request preparation,
native work, cache publication, and all later managed records are suppressed.
Stage identity/order/timing, pass configuration and sequence identity,
`CompileOptions` identity, caller immutability, independent compilation, and
cache identity remain unchanged on successful paths.

| P2 | Same producer and spelling for multiply | Same type, ownership, dormant caller, consumers, and generic rewrite exposure as P1. Rejected with the complete post-op pair. |
| M1 | `CINLowerer.get_level_arrays`: `<tensor>_mode_indices[level][0].data_ptr<int>()` | Fresh compressed-position `VarInit.value`, `PTR_INT`, borrowed from the by-value nested Torch-tensor ABI container. Live input ABI assembly. It requires two structured subscripts plus a templated member call. Selected only with the complete M1-M4 receiver-call family. |
| M2 | Same producer with `[1].data_ptr<int>()` | Fresh compressed-coordinate `PTR_INT`; same live borrowed ABI ownership and representation requirement as M1. Selected with M1-M4. |
| M3 | Same producer: `<tensor>_mode_indices[level][0]` | Fresh coordinate-tensor `VarInit.value`, `TORCH_TENSOR`, copied from the nested container. Live, but M4 repeats the same selection and derives its pointer, so M3 alone is not a complete production family. Selected with M1-M4. |
| M4 | Same producer: `<tensor>_mode_indices[level][0].data_ptr<int>()` | Fresh coordinate-pointer `PTR_INT`, borrowed from the selected Torch tensor. Live and coupled to the same nested receiver-call representation as M1/M2. Selected with M1-M4. |
| W0 | `lower_TensorAccess`: `<tensor>_val[physical_index]` | Returned metadata-free `TensorAccess` rvalue, `NO_TYPE`. Supported production lowering takes the structured physical-access route and this fallback spelling is inconsistent with workspace storage. Nonactivating; rejected. |
| D1 | Workspace initialization: `<workspace>[tile_size]` | Fresh `VarInit.var` with the workspace scalar type. This is a live stack-array declarator, not an rvalue access; migration requires generalized allocation/declarator target work. Rejected. |
| W1 | Untiled workspace copy: `<workspace>[loop_var]` | Fresh `Assign.value`, `NO_TYPE`, borrowing local workspace storage. Direct internal CIN can construct it, but supported scheduled dense workspaces take `memcpy` or the already structured tiled route. Rejected. |
| C1 | Discarded all-COO pre-scan: `<crd>[_p]` | Fresh `NO_TYPE` comparison operand borrowing an input coordinate pointer. The scalar-accumulator production caller discards this pre-scan tree before emitted LLIR. Rejected. |
| C2 | Same pre-scan: `<crd>[_p - 1]` | Same discarded ownership/path as C1; the subtraction index also needs a coordinated typed child. Rejected. |
| G1 | Discarded all-COO group loop: `_group_starts[_g]` | Fresh `VarInit.value`, `INT64`, promoting an owned `std::vector<int>` element. The grouped tree is discarded and the leaf participates in the legacy bracket-to-`.at(...)` compatibility rewrite. Rejected. |
| G2 | Same group loop: `_group_starts[_g + 1]` | Same discarded vector ownership and rewrite interaction as G1, plus an arithmetic index. Rejected. |
| I1 | Coordinate `ModeIterator` root-begin alternative: `<tensor><level>_pos[0]` | Fresh iterator begin, `INT`. Root coordinate lowering emits literal `0`, so this alternative never reaches generated LLIR. Rejected. |
| I2 | Coordinate `ModeIterator` root-end alternative: `<tensor><level>_pos[1]` | Fresh iterator end, `INT`. Root coordinate lowering derives `.size(0)`, so this alternative never reaches generated LLIR. Rejected. |

The other 13 direct expressions were audited independently rather than counted
as additional subscripts:

| IDs | Category and opaque spelling | Producer, consumer, type, ownership, reachability, rewrite interaction, and decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| K1/K2 | Calls: `<result>_values_torch.data_ptr<T>()` | Dense-capacity and known-NNZ result pointer `VarInit.value` leaves with exact pointer types. Live final Torch ABI, borrowing the result tensor. Once exact receiver-call support was required by M1-M4, these were selected to avoid retaining a second opaque representation of the same operation. |
| K3 | Call: `<input>_values.data_ptr<T>()` | Fresh live input value-pointer `VarInit.value` with the exact scalar-pointer type, borrowing the input Torch tensor. Selected with the exact `data_ptr<T>()` family. |
| K4/K5 | Calls: `<coordinate_tensor>.data_ptr<int>()` and `<value_tensor>.data_ptr<T>()` | Fresh intermediate pointer `VarInit.value` leaves with exact types. Live through applicable managed passes, but no pass parsed the opaque member-call spelling. Selected with the same receiver-call family. |
| K6 | Call: `<post_op>_values.data_ptr<T>()` | Fresh post-op tensor pointer with the exact scalar-pointer type. Live post-op ABI extraction. Selected with the same receiver-call family. |
| K7/K8 | Calls: `<schedule_storage>.data()` | Fresh exact-pointer `VarInit.value` leaves for heap-result-tile and packed-operand relayout storage. Live only with the corresponding explicit schedule plan. Selected because the exact receiver-call node already represented K1-K6; their owning vector types remain exact. |
| B1 | Member: `<result>.storage.index.mode_indices` | Fresh live result-assembler `Assign.var`. Selected as an exact nested `MemberAccess` lvalue and coupled to N3. |
| B2 | Member: `<result>.storage.value` | Fresh live result-assembler `Assign.var`. Selected as the matching exact nested storage lvalue. |
| B3 | Member: `<input>.storage.value` | Fresh input-storage `VarInit.value`, `TORCH_TENSOR`. Dormant compatibility read, selected through the same exact storage-member builder so the storage path has one representation. |
| N3 | Initializer: nested textual mode-index braces | Fresh live result `mode_indices` assignment value. Selected as nested typed `Array` nodes with B1; leaving it opaque would keep the selected result-storage assignment structurally incomplete. |
| T1 | Ternary: `<outer_end> > 0 ? 1 : 0` | Fresh `INT64` initializer in the discarded all-COO group-preparation route. Non-emitting and requires a dedicated conditional expression. Rejected. |

M1-M4 are the only complete live remaining subscript family. M3 by itself
would leave the same receiver spelling opaque at M4; M1, M2, and M4 cannot be
represented by `ArrayAccess` alone because their selected tensor is the
receiver of `data_ptr<int>()`. The smallest representation prerequisite for
M1-M4 was therefore one exact receiver-call expression, not a batch migration
of every remaining subscript. `FunctionCall("receiver.member", ...)` was
rejected because it would hide receiver structure in a callee string;
`GetTensorProperty` has different semantics; parsing old names and a generalized
member/call hierarchy were also rejected. The resulting work changes no C++
ABI signature, storage layout, or source spelling.

The committed implementation then went beyond that required M1-M4
prerequisite: it also migrated K1-K8 and the B1-B3/N3 member/initializer seams.
The governing task explicitly required those families to remain separate, and
their migration was not necessary merely to make M1-M4 representable. The
implementation rationale was to avoid two production representations after
`MemberCall` existed and to make the final storage assignment structurally
complete, but that rationale does not erase the scope-boundary deviation. This
handoff records the deviation explicitly rather than presenting the complete
commit as the requested smallest narrow family. The already-created commits
remain ordered and unrevised as required; any decision to forward-revert or
split their behavior must be a separately authorized follow-up.

#### Representation, traversal, ownership, and compatibility audit

`MemberCall(base, member, template_args, args)` is an exact frozen expression
node. Construction validates an LLIR expression receiver, an identifier member,
exact `DataType` template arguments, and LLIR expression arguments. Caller
lists or tuples are snapshotted to owned tuples. Structural equality and hashing
cover receiver, member, template arguments, and arguments. Common walking visits
the receiver before arguments in deterministic order; common rewriting rebuilds
detached nodes, remains repeatable, and owns replacements. Forged fields,
unknown expression children, unknown subclasses, and non-tuple post-construction
state fail closed with exact indexed diagnostic paths. Codegen treats member
calls as postfix expressions and emits byte-exact
`receiver.member<T>(arguments)` with the required receiver parentheses.

The existing immutable `ArrayAccess` remains the nested mode-index
representation. Its constructor, optional provenance, structural
equality/hashing, deterministic array-then-index traversal, detached rewriting,
unknown-child/subclass failure, and postfix precedence were re-audited before
reuse. A new exact `STD_VECTOR_TORCH_TENSOR` type represents one inner
`std::vector<torch::Tensor>` and remains distinct from the existing
`STD_VECTOR_2D_TORCH_TENSOR` ABI argument type.

`AssignmentTarget` is now exactly `Var | MemberAccess | ArrayAccess`. A
structured member lvalue must be an exact chain of exact `MemberAccess` nodes
rooted in an exact metadata-free `Var` whose name is one identifier and whose
type is a `DataType`. Unknown subclasses, call receivers, array receivers,
metadata-bearing roots, and forged members fail at construction, traversal, or
codegen as appropriate. Existing dotted-`Var` assignment targets remain
deliberately accepted by the legacy compatibility grammar: the canonical suite
proved that generated loop-invariant wrappers still rely on that narrow path.
This slice therefore does not claim that every dotted assignment spelling has
already migrated.

`torch_cpp_abi.py` contains only three focused expression builders:

- `mode_index_tensor(name, level, slot)` creates a fresh nested
  `ArrayAccess(ArrayAccess(Var(STD_VECTOR_2D_TORCH_TENSOR), Literal(INT)),
  Literal(INT))`;
- `tensor_data_ptr(receiver, T)` creates a typed templated `MemberCall`; and
- `tensor_storage_member(name, *members)` creates a fresh nested member chain
  rooted at `Var(TACO_TENSOR)`.

They validate boundary inputs and return fresh child objects on every call.
They do not own validation calls, result allocation, `ResultTensorAssembler`,
or a broader TorchCppABI object.

The migrated producers are exact:

- M1/M2/M4 use `tensor_data_ptr(mode_index_tensor(...), INT)`; M3 uses the
  independently owned `mode_index_tensor(...)` value;
- K1-K6 use `tensor_data_ptr(...)` with exact Torch-tensor receivers and exact
  scalar template types; together with M1/M2/M4 this is nine production helper
  calls;
- K7/K8 use exact `MemberCall(..., "data")` nodes whose receivers have the
  corresponding scalar `std::vector<T>` type;
- B1/B2/B3 use `tensor_storage_member(...)`; final result values and returns
  now carry exact `TORCH_TENSOR` and `TACO_TENSOR` types; and
- N3 is an outer `Array(STD_VECTOR_2D_TORCH_TENSOR)` containing one fresh inner
  `Array(STD_VECTOR_TORCH_TENSOR)` per result level and exact Torch-tensor
  leaves for compressed or coordinate storage.

All applicable managed passes use the common traversal and rebuild these nodes
without parsing emitted syntax. The ten generic string rewrites remain ten and
none parses a migrated spelling. Dynamic-vector assignment deduplication
considers only adjacent equal indexed `Assign(ASSIGN)` writes to declared
dynamic coordinate vectors; it cannot consume these `VarInit` member calls or
the result storage-member targets. Equality at that seam remains structural and
metadata-independent where the existing node contracts require it.

A forged `MemberCall` appended after result assembly preserves the exact
successful sparse-prefetch, dense-pointer, single-iteration, and
loop-invariant-factor record prefix, then fails in the owning dynamic-vector
rewrite with a managed partial record. Schedule lowering, C++ generation,
build/request preparation, native load, cache publication, and all later work
are suppressed. Stage identity/order/timing, exact `CompileOptions` identity,
caller-owned input immutability, cache identity, independent compilation, and
failure-state suppression remain locked on real production paths.

`ResultTensorAssembler` intentionally remains in `cin_lowerer.py`, and the
compressed-result W15 compound raw statement remains raw. This slice does not
begin full TorchCppABI extraction, generalized member/call hierarchy work,
parsing, generalized allocation/declarator migration, parallel zero-fill
extraction, DCE, Phase 3.5, or LoopIR.

#### Locked post-slice compatibility budget

The production budget is now:

- 379 total `Var` constructors;
- 12 direct expression strings: 11 subscript and one ternary;
- 367 other constructor arguments, including the same 11 known indirect
  sinks/clones;
- ten generic string rewrites;
- 38 `RawStmt` constructors / 37 semantic producers;
- nine `tensor_data_ptr`, four `mode_index_tensor`, and three
  `tensor_storage_member` production calls;
- four production `MemberCall` constructor templates: one focused helper, two
  schedule producers, and one common-traversal rebuild;
- no direct opaque call, member, initializer, qualified, or arithmetic
  expression in a production `Var.name`;
- no `std::move(` in a production `Var.name`; and
- no direct string-expression `Assign` target.

The remaining direct subscripts are exactly P1/P2, W0, D1, W1, C1/C2, G1/G2,
and I1/I2: nine sites in `cin_lowerer.py` and two in `iterator.py`. T1 is the
single remaining ternary in `cin_lowerer.py`. `FunctionCall` still deliberately
owns string callee identities such as `std::move` and `std::lower_bound`, and
legacy dotted-`Var` targets remain accepted; the budget statement is limited to
direct expression syntax hidden in production `Var.name` values.

D1 was therefore the sole live site. P1/P2, W0/W1, and I1/I2 have no
successful supported public activation; C1/C2 and G1/G2 are constructed but
discarded. Existing `ArrayAccess` remains the right representation for actual
element access, but reusing it for D1 would conflate an expression with a
declaration.

The chosen boundary takes the useful LLVM/Clang/MLIR distinction—storage
declaration is a statement, element access is an expression, and neither is
encoded in a symbol name—without importing any compiler's generalized
allocation system. The transitional production form is exactly:

```python
llir.FixedStackArrayDecl(
    name="wksp",
    element_type=llir.DataType.FLOAT32,
    extent=llir.Var("kTile_k", llir.DataType.CONSTEXPR_INT),
    initializer=llir.Array([], llir.DataType.FLOAT32),
)
```

It adds one statement node and one production constructor. It changes no ABI,
signature, storage layout, `AssignmentTarget`, or `ArrayAccess` contract and
adds no parser, heap allocation, arbitrary declarator, generalized call/member
hierarchy, or other prohibited expansion.

#### Representation, traversal, ownership, and compatibility audit

- `llir.py:601-685` defines the frozen structural statement. Supported element
  types are exactly `FLOAT32`, `FLOAT64`, `INT32`, `INT64`, `INT8`, and
  `UINT8`.
- The extent is either an exact metadata-free, non-pointer, non-restrict
  identifier `Var(CONSTEXPR_INT)` or a positive integral `Literal` typed
  `INT`, `INT32`, `INT64`, `UINT32`, or `UINT64`. Dynamic extents, heap
  storage, multidimensional arrays, alignment, and arbitrary initializers are
  deliberately outside the node.
- The initializer must be an exact empty `Array` whose type is identical to
  the element type. `Array` snapshots the caller sequence into an owned tuple.
  `TileSizeVar.llir_var` at `cin.py:515-517` supplies a fresh exact extent on
  every production access. The parent is frozen and structurally equal/hashable;
  because legacy `Var` remains mutable, the guarantee is fresh child ownership
  and detached rewriting rather than deep transitive immutability.
- Exact statement registration is at `llir_traversal.py:76-82`; forged-field
  validation is at `:371-441`. Deterministic walk order is extent then
  initializer at `:938-945`. Detached rewriting follows the same order,
  validates replacements, and builds a fresh parent at `:1668-1733`.
  Unknown children and non-exact subclasses fail closed.
- Codegen first takes the common validation walk and then emits
  `T name[extent] = {};` at `codegen.py:125-138`. Admitted extents are primary
  expressions, so no wider declarator-precedence grammar is introduced. The
  locked production bytes remain exactly `float wksp[kTile_k] = {};`.
- `AssignmentTarget` remains exactly `Var | MemberAccess | ArrayAccess`.
  Existing `ArrayAccess` construction, validation, precedence, equality,
  ownership, traversal, and rewriting are unchanged.
- The loop-invariant defined-name collector records the fixed declaration at
  `loop_invariant_factor_pass.py:215-228`, so workspace reads cannot be
  misclassified as invariant. Schedule name hygiene recursively records it at
  `schedule_lowerer.py:353-370`, preventing packed-storage name collisions.
- Dynamic-vector discovery intentionally still recognizes only `VarDecl`, and
  assignment deduplication still considers only adjacent qualifying `Assign`
  stores. A fixed stack array is neither and does not perturb either seam.
- The global registry's seven managed pass identities and order remain
  unchanged. The production paths audited for this slice execute their usual
  five-pass subset. Common traversal validates and detaches the node;
  specialized compatibility passes otherwise leave it alone. The ten locked
  generic string-rewrite markers remain ten, and none parses
  `FixedStackArrayDecl.name`.
- A malformed declaration created inside `lower_Where` fails during the first
  owning sparse-prefetch traversal, records no completed LLIR pass, and
  suppresses result-ABI work, schedule lowering, C++ generation, build
  preparation, native loading, and cache publication. A malformed declaration
  appended after body assembly preserves the exact four-pass
  sparse-prefetch/dense-pointer/single-iteration/factor prefix, then fails in
  the owning dynamic-vector traversal and suppresses every later stage.

- no direct opaque call, member, initializer, qualified, or separately

- no `std::move(` in a production `Var.name`; and
- no direct string-expression `Assign` target.

The ten remaining subscripts are exactly P1/P2, W0, W1, C1/C2, G1/G2, and

#### Complete pre-implementation inventory and selection

The post-fixed-stack budget contained ten direct subscript spellings and one
ternary. Every site was re-audited at exact base `d5e0720` by producer,
consumer, exact type, ownership, source spelling, production reachability, and
compatibility-rewrite interaction:

| IDs | Producer and type | Ownership, reachability, and consumers | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1/P2 | `_emit_post_ops` add/multiply RHS, `NO_TYPE` | Fresh leaves borrowing an extra-tensor value pointer. Their only production-source caller is W1; dense-pointer and generic string rewrites would inspect them before codegen. | Dormant and inseparable from the unsupported `_post_ops`/W1 contract; rejected. |
| W0 | `lower_TensorAccess` workspace fallback, `NO_TYPE` | Borrowed workspace storage. Reached only when tensor metadata is absent; supported workspace paths use specialized lowering, and this fallback's `<workspace>_val[...]` spelling does not match actual storage. | Latent wrong-code fallback; a future contract decision should fail it closed, not structure it. |
| W1 | Untiled dense-workspace copy RHS, `NO_TYPE` | Borrowed local storage. Requires a dense untiled workspace whose corresponding result level is not dense, while scheduler construction derives workspace density from those same result levels. | Scheduler-unreachable; reject with P1/P2. |
| C1/C2 | All-COO pre-scan coordinate reads, `NO_TYPE` | Borrowed `int*`; C2 also embeds `_p - 1`. Production constructs the pre-scan only on a scalar-accumulation route that then selects the flat branch and discards it. | Dead final-tree construction and arithmetic-coupled; rejected. |
| G1/G2 | `_group_starts[_g]` and `_group_starts[_g + 1]`, `INT64` | Elements of a locally owned `std::vector<int>`. The same discarded group route is their only source; if activated, dynamic-vector rewriting must preserve checked `.at(...)` behavior. | Dead and rewrite-coupled; plain `ArrayAccess` would be wrong. |
| I1/I2 | Root-coordinate placeholder begin/end, `INT` | Borrowed position storage, but emitted initialization uses literal zero and `crd_tensor.size(0)` instead. Neither placeholder enters a statement tree or traversal. | Semantically obsolete placeholders; leave for iterator cleanup/LoopIR. |
| T1 | `outer_end > 0 ? 1 : 0`, `INT64` | Fresh opaque leaf used only by the same discarded grouped all-COO pre-scan. No conditional expression node exists; `IfThenElse` is statement-only. | A byte-exact migration requires the design's general conditional node, precedence, traversal, and manual-rewriter support. Rejected for a non-surviving producer. |

Thus no remaining string-expression family is a supported live final-LLIR
candidate. Migrating one would improve only the lexical budget, not production
semantics. Deleting the grouped route would be prohibited DCE, and adding a
general conditional solely for T1 would be an unjustified hierarchy expansion.

The Phase-3 exit audit instead identified the complete
`ResultTensorAssembler` family as the smallest coherent live production seam.
At the base it retained a mutable semantic `TensorVar` and owned all of the
following concrete Torch/C++ boundary work inside `cin_lowerer.py`:

| Producer family | Inputs and output | Consumers and activation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `emit_value_array_init` | Dense capacity/product and `torch::empty`, known-NNZ Torch storage, or dynamic `std::vector`; also the existing `scorch_zero_dense` call | Invoked for every non-workspace result and re-invoked for the known-NNZ route before the managed pipeline barrier. |
| `emit_level_indices_init` | Dense/compressed/coordinate position and coordinate buffers, reserve hints, structured zero-position assignment | Invoked with each value initializer; statements are traversed and rewritten by the managed LLIR pipeline. |
| `_get_mode_index_set` | Fresh tuple-owned structured Torch mode-index arrays | Consumed only by final result assembly. |
| `emit_final_assembly` | Typed vector moves, mode-index/value storage assignments, and return construction | Invoked exactly once in nested `RESULT_ABI_ASSEMBLY` unless the owning compressed-output route suppresses later assembly. |

The three base construction sites all belonged to this one family: initial
value/index setup, known-NNZ reassembly, and final result assembly. Kernel
argument construction, validation calls, function signature construction,
parallel zero-fill policy, allocation generalization, and post-op ABI remain
separate later seams. Moving this family changes ownership and dependency
direction without changing the generated ABI or C++ spelling.

#### Representation, ownership, and dependency result

`ResultTensorAssembler` now lives in `torch_cpp_abi.py` as a frozen dataclass.
It owns only a validated result name, immutable `Tuple[LevelType, ...]`,
`torch.dtype`, and optional known-NNZ/fixed-parent/reserve policy values.
`levels` and density are derived from that immutable tuple. It no longer owns or
imports `TensorVar`; `torch_cpp_abi.py` has no dependency on CIN or
`CINLowerer`.

`CINLowerer` has one `_result_tensor_abi_assembler` boundary that snapshots the
semantic tensor into those ABI values. Its three existing call positions and
the lazy `LLIRBodyAssembler` continuation remain in place. The nested result-ABI
stage, managed pass order, partial/failure records, later-stage suppression,
and caller-owned artifacts are unchanged.

An independent AST review found `_has_fixed_position_count`,
`emit_level_indices_init`, `_get_mode_index_set`, and `emit_final_assembly`
identical to the base. `emit_value_array_init` differs only by reading dense
rank from the frozen `self.levels` snapshot instead of mutable
`self.tensor_var.levels`. The legacy import identity still aliases the exact
extracted class. No blocker was found.

Focused tests lock malformed names/layout tuples/dtypes/options, exact metadata
types, frozen assignment failure, structural equality and hashing, independence
from later `TensorVar` name/format/dtype mutation, detached repeated emission,
byte-exact dense/known-NNZ/sparse assembly, module ownership, one production
construction boundary, and absence of a reverse CIN import. Existing stage
tests now monkeypatch the extracted class rather than a stale location.

#### Complete pre-implementation inventory and selection

The exact-base lexical budget already contained only ten direct subscript
spellings and one ternary. The prior result-ABI audit proved that none was a
supported live final-LLIR family: two post-op leaves depend on a dormant
workspace route, one workspace fallback has the wrong storage contract, the
all-COO pre-scan/group leaves and ternary are discarded, two iterator
placeholders never enter a statement tree, and the vector-backed group leaves
require the existing checked-access compatibility rewrite. Structuring one of
them would either migrate dead spelling, perform prohibited DCE, or require a
new conditional/generalized hierarchy.

The later explicit recommendation review therefore selected one LLVM-like
target boundary: freeze semantic kernel metadata once, then let the existing
Torch/C++ ABI layer materialize the public signature, validation, input
prologue, post-op pointers, and final function wrapper. This is one live family
for every generated outer kernel and does not change the ABI. The complete
exact-base producer/consumer inventory was:

| Family | Exact base producer and inputs | Output, ownership, reachability, and consumer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Result contract | `final_result_tensor_var or result_tensor_var`: mutable name, optional shape, level list, dtype | Supplies expected result shape/rank to the public validator. Live for every outer `evaluate`; runtime supplies the physical result shape by value. |
| Input contracts | Ordered `stmt.get_rhs_tensor_vars()`: mutable name, levels, optional mode order/shape, dtype | Supplies every public input triple and its validation/prologue. Workspace result temporaries are not RHS ABI arguments. Live D/S/O paths consume the generated extent/index/value locals. |
| Public arguments | Inline `kernel_args`: `result_shape`, then shape/mode-index/value for every RHS tensor, then `PostOps.extra_tensors` | Fresh caller-by-value `llir.Var` arguments consumed by `llir.Function`, schedule lowering, codegen, and the existing `module.evaluate(*args)` packers. |
| Result validation | Inline `validate_jit_result_shape` `RawStmt` | First body statement; validates expected extents/rank before any result subscript. Native support code consumes the exact rendered call. |
| Input validation | Local level-code map, `_cpp_int_vector`, and one `validate_jit_tensor` `RawStmt` per RHS tensor | Validates dtype, D/S/O code tuple, physical mode order, and known physical shape before nested mode-index access or `data_ptr`. The by-value mode-index vector may be replaced locally with checked int32 tensors without mutating the caller. |
| Extra validation | One `validate_jit_extra_tensor` `RawStmt` per post-op extra | Uses the final-result dtype and preserves extra order. Live add/multiply post-op kernels consume the validated tensor. |
| Dense input level | `get_level_arrays`: `INT64` `VarInit` from existing structured `N_shape[level]` | Fresh local extent, owned by the lowered body and consumed by loop bounds. Live for every D level. |
| Compressed input level | `get_level_arrays`: restrict `PTR_INT` position/coordinate `VarInit` values from structured `N_mode_indices[level][slot].data_ptr<int>()` | Fresh local pointers borrowing caller-owned Torch tensors. Live for every S level and consumed by sparse iteration. |
| Coordinate input level | `get_level_arrays`: Torch coordinate handle plus restrict `PTR_INT` from slot zero | Fresh local handle/pointer borrowing caller storage. Live for every O level. |
| Input values | `get_val_ptr_stmt`: dtype-specific restrict pointer from `N_values.data_ptr<T>()` | Fresh local pointer borrowing the input value tensor; live for every RHS tensor and consumed by loads. |
| Extra values | Inline post-op loop: dtype-specific restrict pointer from `E_values.data_ptr<T>()` | Fresh local pointer borrowing the extra tensor; live only when an extra is present and consumed by post-op assignments. |
| Function wrapper | Inline `llir.Function(TACO_TENSOR, "evaluate", kernel_args, body_stmts)` after the managed pipeline | Owns a fresh argument list and compiler-owned body container; schedule lowering and `LLIRLowerer` consume it. Live once per outer kernel. |

The exact public argument schema remains:

1. `result_shape: STD_VECTOR_INT` (`std::vector<int64_t>`);
2. for every RHS tensor, in collector order,
   `N_shape: STD_VECTOR_INT`,
   `N_mode_indices: STD_VECTOR_2D_TORCH_TENSOR`, and
   `N_values: TORCH_TENSOR`; then
3. every `E_values: TORCH_TENSOR` in `PostOps.extra_tensors` order.

All arguments remain by value with no pointer/restrict/access metadata. The
function remains `Tensor evaluate(...)` with LLIR return type `TACO_TENSOR`.
The existing normal, cached-dispatch, and direct-CIN runtime packers already
supply result shape followed by each input triple; the normal post-op path then
appends extras. No runtime packing, cache, `ops.py`, or public ABI changed.

The coherent family was selected because it has one semantic snapshot point,
one target-specific owner, one public ordering contract, complete live
activation, and existing structured LLIR children. It required no parser,
generalized member/call hierarchy, or allocation representation. The following
remained separate and were rejected from this slice:

- `ResultTensorAssembler` allocation, mode-index/result storage, and final
  return assembly, whose existing frozen ownership was already complete;
- compressed-output allocation/fill/final assembly and parallel zero-fill;
- generalized allocation, emitter, CxxIR, or build-spec work;
- the ten dead/latent/rewrite-coupled subscript spellings and discarded
  ternary;
- runtime argument packing or native validator implementation changes;
- parsing, DCE, and unrelated scheduling/optimization work; and
- Phase 3.5, the LoopIR feasibility spike, and LoopIR itself.

#### Representation, validation, ownership, and exact spelling

`torch_cpp_abi.py` now owns two frozen exact dataclasses:

- `KernelTensorABI(name, level_types, mode_order, shape, dtype)`; and
- `TorchCppKernelABI(result_shape, result_rank, input_tensors,
  extra_tensor_names, extra_tensor_dtype, function_name="evaluate")`.

`CINLowerer._kernel_tensor_abi` converts mutable semantic input metadata to
immutable tuples. `_torch_cpp_kernel_abi` snapshots the result, ordered inputs,
and ordered post-op extras once at the outer non-recursive lowering boundary.
Neither object retains a `TensorVar`, `PostOps`, CIN node, or mutable semantic
container. `torch_cpp_abi.py` imports neither `cin` nor `cin_lowerer`; the
dependency remains one-way from semantic lowering to the target ABI layer.

The former producers map exactly as follows:

| Former owner | Frozen ABI owner |
| --- | --- |
| `CINLowerer.get_level_arrays` | `KernelTensorABI.emit_level_array_bindings` |
| `CINLowerer.get_val_ptr_stmt` | `KernelTensorABI.emit_value_pointer` |
| Manual per-input comment/prologue loop | `TorchCppKernelABI.emit_input_prologue` |
| Inline `kernel_args` construction | `TorchCppKernelABI.emit_arguments` |
| Local `_cpp_int_vector`, level-code map, and three validator families | ABI `_cpp_int_vector`, `KernelTensorABI._level_kind_codes`, and `TorchCppKernelABI.emit_validation` |
| Inline extra-pointer loop | `TorchCppKernelABI.emit_extra_tensor_prologue` |
| Inline function constructor | `TorchCppKernelABI.assemble_function` |

Valid source spelling remains byte-for-byte:

```cpp
int64_t N0_size = N_shape[0];
int* __restrict__ N1_pos = N_mode_indices[1][0].data_ptr<int>();
int* __restrict__ N1_crd = N_mode_indices[1][1].data_ptr<int>();
torch::Tensor N0_crd_tensor = N_mode_indices[0][0];
T* __restrict__ N_val = N_values.data_ptr<T>();
T* __restrict__ E_val = E_values.data_ptr<T>();
```

The three validator families retain exact names, comma/space spelling, D/S/O
codes `0/1/2`, and `{}` for an unknown compile-time shape. All subscripts reuse
the existing `ArrayAccess`; all `data_ptr<T>()` calls reuse the existing
`MemberCall`. No new node hierarchy was introduced.

Construction and every public emission method reject malformed or forged
fields: non-identifiers; mutable/wrong-element tuples; unsupported singleton
levels; non-permutation mode orders; known shape/rank mismatch; negative
extents; wrong dtypes; subclass/unknown tensor snapshots; inconsistent extra
dtype ownership; duplicate/colliding generated argument names; and a non-list
function body. Empty shape remains the intentional runtime-shaped contract.
Exact-int and permutation checks tighten only malformed direct/internal callers
that bypass public `STensor`/`TensorSpec` normalization; no valid production
ABI or source changes.

Every emission produces fresh LLIR nodes. Frozen snapshots compare and hash
structurally, but repeated emissions have disjoint identity. The function owns
a fresh argument list and a copied outer body container. Mutating the source
tensor's name, format, shape, mode order, dtype, or post-op list later cannot
change the snapshot. Nested body ownership remains the existing compiler-owned
pass artifact contract.

#### Traversal, pass, rewrite, deduplication, and failure audit

The snapshot and prologue/validation statements are created inside inclusive
`CIN_LOWERING` before recursive body lowering. The existing body-assembly
continuation inserts them after sparse-prefetch, dense-pointer-hoist,
single-iteration, and loop-invariant-factor work, while nested
`RESULT_ABI_ASSEMBLY` is active. Dynamic-vector rewriting then traverses,
validates, and detaches the assembled statements. `assemble_function` runs
after dynamic rewriting and the nested child stage, still inside CIN lowering;
optional schedule lowering and C++ emission remain downstream.

This preserves the exact ordinary and compressed-output body ordering:

1. result/input/extra validation;
2. result-level sizes;
3. ordered input prologue;
4. route-specific result/tile work;
5. post-op pointers;
6. recursive compute; and
7. ordinary final result assembly only when the compressed-output owner has not
   already emitted it.

The first four ordinary passes and the compressed-output transform operate on
the recursive body before these ABI statements are inserted. Dynamic-vector is
the only managed pass that traverses them. Its bracket-in-name compatibility
rewrite does not match any moved identifier; its vector discovery accepts
`VarDecl`, while these declarations are `VarInit`; and its adjacent dynamic
coordinate assignment deduplication sees no moved `Assign`. Raw validation
spelling is unchanged. Function arguments are constructed after that pass.
The same ten generic string-rewrite sites remain; no compatibility parser or
assignment-dedup behavior changed.

Failure timing is explicit:

- snapshot, input-prologue, validation, and extra-prologue failures publish no
  completed CIN/result-ABI record, retain the outer prefix through legacy CIN
  adaptation, record no managed LLIR pass, leave both caches empty, and suppress
  schedule lowering, C++ generation, request construction, and native loading;
- dynamic-vector failure retains the completed nested result-ABI record and the
  four preceding ordinary pass records, but no dynamic/CIN completion; and
- function-wrapper failure retains the completed nested result-ABI record and
  all five ordinary pass records, but no CIN completion or later stage.

All preserve the original exception identity. Successful stage identities,
order, nesting/timing, `CompileOptions` identity, sequence indices, cache keys,
caller-owned immutability, and independent compilation remain unchanged.

The DS compressed-output activation monkeypatches ordinary
`ResultTensorAssembler.emit_final_assembly` to fail, proving that its pass-owned
final result suppresses ordinary assembly. Its public contract is
`SparseProduct`, both real RHS tensors are validated, and no workspace enters
the public signature or validator.

#### Complete pre-implementation inventory and selection

The exact-base lexical budget contained ten direct subscript spellings and one
ternary. Every site was re-audited by producer, consumer, type, ownership,
production reachability, source spelling, and generic-rewrite interaction:

| IDs | Producer, spelling, and type | Ownership, reachability, consumers, and rewrite interaction | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1/P2 | `_emit_post_ops` add/multiply leaves, `<extra>_val[index_expr]`, `NO_TYPE` | Fresh reads borrowing an extra-tensor pointer. Their only caller is the unsupported untiled workspace-copy fallback. If activated, dense-pointer and generated-name compatibility scans can inspect the flat spelling. | Dormant and inseparable from W1; rejected. |
| W0 | Generic `lower_TensorAccess`, `<workspace>_val[physical_index]`, `NO_TYPE` | Fresh metadata-free value read. `_tensor_access_metadata` returns `None` exactly for a workspace. Supported workspace producers and consumers use `lower_TensorAssign` and `lower_ConsumerIndexStmt`; actual storage is `wksp[...]` or structured pair members, not `<workspace>_val[...]`. Direct CIN construction could nevertheless emit invalid C++ and scalar access could fail first with `IndexError`. | Selected as a fail-closed legality boundary, not as a structured live-expression migration. |
| W1 | Untiled workspace element-copy RHS, `<workspace>[loop_var]`, `NO_TYPE` | Fresh read from local storage. Supported scheduled dense workspaces return through `memcpy` or the structured tiled path. P1/P2 are applied only here. | Scheduler-unreachable and coupled to the dormant post-op family; rejected. |
| C1/C2 | Discarded all-COO pre-scan, `<crd>[_p]` and `<crd>[_p - 1]`, `NO_TYPE` | Borrowed `int*` reads. The scalar-accumulation production route constructs this group pre-scan and then selects the flat route, so the tree never reaches final LLIR. C2 also needs structured arithmetic in the index. | Non-emitting and arithmetic-coupled; rejected rather than performing DCE. |
| G1/G2 | Discarded all-COO group loop, `_group_starts[_g]` and `_group_starts[_g + 1]`, `INT64` | Reads from an owned `std::vector<int>`. The dynamic-vector pass would have to preserve checked `.at(...)` reads if this dormant route became live. | Non-emitting and compatibility-rewrite-coupled; rejected. |
| I1/I2 | Coordinate iterator alternatives, `<tensor>_pos[0]` and `[1]`, `INT` | Borrowed position bounds. Production root-coordinate initialization instead uses literal zero and structured `crd_tensor.size(0)`; these placeholder values never enter a statement tree. | Obsolete non-tree placeholders; retained for later iterator/LoopIR work. |
| T1 | Discarded all-COO pre-scan, `outer_end > 0 ? 1 : 0`, `INT64` | Fresh conditional value used only by the discarded group route. Current LLIR has statement conditionals but no conditional expression. | Requires a generalized conditional node for non-emitting code; rejected. |

W0 is the smallest allowed production-relevant safety seam. It is analogous to
an LLVM dialect-conversion legality check: reject an operation at the boundary
whose semantic owner is known instead of letting malformed target text escape.
It requires no ABI change, parser, new expression hierarchy, allocation or
parallel representation, DCE, optimization change, Phase 3.5 work, or LoopIR.

Emitter closure was separately rejected. Common traversal currently accepts
`GetTensorProperty`, `Allocate`, `Free`, `Print`, `Case`, and `Switch` while
common codegen rejects them, but none has a live production producer. Emitting
`Allocate` would cross the prohibited generalized-allocation boundary; pruning
the schema or deleting the unused `llir.CppCodeGenerator` would be prohibited
DCE rather than a production seam.

All ten generic string rewrites were also inventoried before editing:

| Owner and locked sites | Current production role and decision |
| --- | --- |
| `cin_lowerer.py`, two `_rewrite_val_refs` call/raw fields | Rewrites `<array>[` to `<array>.data()[` under a grouped all-COO branch. Structured `ArrayAccess` bases have a separate rewrite. The lexical call/raw branch is production-unreachable once known NNZ is established; deleting it now would be DCE-like and unrelated to W0. |
| `compressed_where_openmp_pass.py`, three workspace-insert Var/call/raw fields | The exact `wksp.insert` `FunctionCallStmt` producer is live and must become `wksp.insert_unchecked`; Var and raw forms are compatibility-only. This is the best next narrow generic-rewrite seam: exact call-name matching can replace broad substring rewriting without a hierarchy or parser. |
| `dense_pointer_hoist_pass.py`, two call/raw fields | Live tensor reads use structured `ArrayAccess`; production call names and current raw producers do not carry the matched word-index spelling. The two fields are compatibility-only and remain separate cleanup. |
| `dynamic_vector_access_pass.py`, one regex Var-name field | The only current opaque reads are dormant G1/G2. A principled live migration needs read-versus-lvalue context and an existing `MemberCall(.at, index)` rewrite; simple deletion would weaken future checked reads. |
| `single_iteration_loop_pass.py`, two call/raw fields | The live all-COO rewrite changes structured `ArrayAccess` indices. Production call/raw fields contain no matching loop token; the compatibility arms remain a separate pair. |

W0 does not feed any of those rewrite fields, so the generic rewrite budget
correctly remains ten. The audit did not group unrelated rewrite cleanup into
this slice.

#### Diagnostic boundary, ownership, and behavior

`CINLowerer.lower_TensorAccess` now snapshots the semantic tensor and asks for
logical access metadata before reading the sorted physical index. A `None`
metadata result therefore raises the exact stage-owned diagnostic:

```text
stage=CIN lowering pass=lower_TensorAccess: workspace tensor '<name>' reached
generic value lowering; workspace reads require a workspace-specific consumer
```

This catches rank-zero workspaces before the former incidental `IndexError` and
indexed workspaces before the former opaque `Var` is constructed. It does not
mutate the `WorkspaceAccess`, its indices, its tensor, the caller-owned CIN, or
managed pass records. The existing specialized workspace producer/consumer
paths are unchanged.

Non-workspace reads still return the same frozen `ArrayAccess` with fresh,
accurately typed value-pointer and physical-index `Var` children plus exact
`TensorAccessMetadata`. Their emitted C++ is byte-identical. Focused tests cover
rank-zero, rank-one dense, and rank-two coordinate workspaces; the exact
diagnostic; direct invalid-workspace-RHS integration; caller immutability; zero
published LLIR pass records; the existing non-workspace positive control; and
an AST lock preventing the opaque fallback from returning.

#### Complete pre-implementation inventory and selection

The exact-base budget contained ten generic string rewrites. Every site was
re-audited by producer, consumed field and type, ownership, production
reachability, source spelling, downstream consumer, and interaction with the
remaining compatibility rewrites:

| Owner and sites | Producer, consumer, ownership, reachability, and spelling | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cin_lowerer.py`, two `_rewrite_val_refs` arms | Detached compatibility traversal mutates `FunctionCallStmt.name` and `RawStmt.code` from `<array>[` to `<array>.data()[`. Structured `ArrayAccess` bases already have a separate typed rewrite. The lexical arms occur only under the discarded grouped all-COO route once known NNZ selects the live scalar/flat path. | Rejected as production-unreachable DCE-like cleanup and retained as a separate future seam. |
| `compressed_where_openmp_pass.py`, one `Var.name` arm | `_WorkspaceInsertRewriter` recursively cloned expressions and changed any `Var.name` containing `<workspace>.insert`. Codegen would emit that name literally, but no production producer encodes a workspace insertion in a `Var`; the synthetic field could also be an lvalue, array base/index, initializer, or ordinary value. | Rejected and removed: production-dead broad substring mutation, not a semantic insertion operation. |
| `compressed_where_openmp_pass.py`, one `FunctionCallStmt.name` arm | `CINLowerer.lower_TensorAssign` is the sole compiler producer. For a non-dense `WorkspaceAccess`, it creates exact name `<workspace>.insert` with a structured `Array[INT64]` of fresh `INT64` index `Var` children and the lowered RHS expression. Common codegen emits the stored call name and structured arguments verbatim. The compressed-Where pass consumes it only after the workspace declaration is hoisted and duplicates the detached work body into count/fill phases. | **Selected.** It is the only live operation among the three fields and can use exact operation-name equality without an ABI change, parser, or hierarchy. |
| `compressed_where_openmp_pass.py`, one `RawStmt.code` arm | Detached compatibility cloning changed any raw code containing `<workspace>.insert`. No production compiler path emits the workspace insertion as `RawStmt`; codegen would otherwise emit the text verbatim. | Rejected and removed with the dead `Var` arm; raw text remains opaque and unchanged. |
| `dense_pointer_hoist_pass.py`, call/raw arms | Live tensor loads use structured `ArrayAccess`. Current production call names and raw producers do not contain the matched word-index spelling; the two arms remain compatibility-only. | Rejected as a distinct dense-pointer compatibility seam. |
| `dynamic_vector_access_pass.py`, one regex `Var.name` arm | The only current opaque vector reads are dormant all-COO G1/G2. Correct migration must distinguish reads from lvalues and retain checked `.at(index)` member-call semantics. | Rejected because it needs a separate read/lvalue representation decision, not this call-name correction. |
| `single_iteration_loop_pass.py`, call/raw arms | The live all-COO route rewrites typed `ArrayAccess` indices. Production call/raw fields contain no matching loop token; these remain compatibility-only. | Rejected as a separate single-iteration compatibility seam. |

The selected family is therefore exactly one producer/consumer contract:
`lower_TensorAssign` produces a semantic `FunctionCallStmt`, the
compressed-Where owning pass changes the exact operation name when it hoists
that workspace, and common codegen emits the result. The live DS production
route exercises the contract twice, once in each generated count/fill phase.
The nested DSS route is the negative control: its workspace is not hoisted at
that seam, so its two calls retain checked `wksp.insert`.

This is deliberately analogous to an LLVM dialect-conversion legality rule:
identify and rewrite one known operation at its owning boundary, while leaving
unknown text and unrelated operations untouched. Prefix, suffix, further
member, already-rewritten, argument, `Var`, initializer, `ArrayAccess`, and raw
spellings are not the selected operation. Migrating all remaining rewrites,
introducing a generalized member/call hierarchy, parsing opaque strings,
changing the workspace ABI, or broadening recursion would all exceed this
slice and were rejected.

#### Exact rewrite boundary, ownership, and failure behavior

`_WorkspaceInsertRewriter` now accepts only an exact built-in nonempty `str`
for every `FunctionCallStmt.name` that reaches its characterized statement
scope. It renames the call only when:

```text
call.name == f"{workspace_name}.insert"
```

and assigns the exact replacement
`f"{workspace_name}.insert_unchecked"`. There is no substring replacement in
the pass. Malformed `None`, empty, whitespace-only, `str`-subclass, and forged
non-string call names raise the pass-owned
`invalid_workspace_insert_call_name` diagnostic at the exact `name` path.
Malformed call-argument containers and members continue to fail through the
common traversal with their original structured diagnostic and path.

The characterized recursion boundary is unchanged: direct statements,
`ForLoop.body`, and every `IfThenElse` body/branch are visited;
`ForLoopAuto`, `WhileLoop`, and arbitrary nested statement containers are
detached but not searched. The pass does not infer new semantics from those
containers. Exact type checks also preserve fail-closed behavior for unknown
nodes and subclasses rather than silently treating them as known operations.

Every returned mutable LLIR node and expression child is detached from the
caller. Repeated transforms produce mutually disjoint graphs with deterministic
structural snapshots; retained immutable tensor-access metadata keeps its
identity. Nonmatching call names, all `Var.name` values, `RawStmt.code`,
structured expression fields, and source LLIR remain unchanged. The common
rewriter continues to validate and freshly clone the structured call arguments,
so replacement ownership does not alias caller-owned children.

The production-pipeline failure test proves that a malformed consumed name
raises the original `LLIRTraversalError` through `LLIRPassPartialFailure`,
publishes zero completed run records, performs neither count nor fill result
rewriting, skips sparse prefetch, dense-pointer hoisting, single-iteration
elimination, factor hoisting, dynamic-vector rewriting, and body assembly, and
leaves caller-owned LLIR unchanged. The existing 12-position owning-stage
matrix continues to prove partial-record accounting and later-stage
suppression everywhere else.

Generated C++ is byte-for-byte unchanged. The DS source still contains exactly
two `wksp.insert_unchecked(` calls and no checked `wksp.insert(` call; DSS still
contains exactly two checked calls and no unchecked call. Existing common
expression emission retains its structural equality, precedence,
unknown-child, and unknown-subclass coverage. No assignment-deduplication seam
changes: the selected node is a statement call, never an `Assign` target, and
all assignment structure and spelling remain unchanged.

#### Complete pre-implementation inventory and selection

The exact-base budget was reproduced before editing:

- 377 production `Var` constructors;
- ten direct expression strings: nine subscripts and one ternary;
- 367 other constructor arguments, including 11 known indirect sinks/clones;
- seven generic string rewrites;
- 38 `RawStmt` constructors / 37 semantic producers; and
- four `MemberCall` constructor templates.

The 38 raw constructors split exactly as follows:

| File | Constructors |
| --- | ---: |
| `cin_lowerer.py` | 12 |
| `compressed_where_openmp_pass.py` | 15 |
| `torch_cpp_abi.py` | 5 |
| `schedule_lowerer.py` | 3 |
| `dense_pointer_hoist_pass.py` | 1 |
| `sparse_prefetch_pass.py` | 1 |
| `llir_traversal.py` | 1 common reconstruction clone |

Every semantic producer was classified by payload, ownership, production
reachability, consumer, and compatibility interaction:

| IDs | Raw family and decision |
| --- | --- |
| C1 | Fixed-position `std::vector<int>` direct initialization. Live owning allocation; rejected as direct-initialization/generalized allocation work. |
| C2 | Known-NNZ Torch coordinate allocation plus typed `data_ptr<int>()`. Live Torch owner/borrowed pointer pair; rejected as compound Torch allocation/ABI work. |
| C3-C5 | Dense-workspace extent, per-worker pointer, and `memset`. Live coupled workspace family; rejected because completing it begins the prohibited parallel zero-fill/allocation seam. |
| C6 | Dense-workspace `memcpy` into an addressed result subscript. Live, but needs coordinated address/subscript/copy representation and compatibility updates. |
| C7 | Nested templated `_dynamic_reserve` policy. Live, but coupled to allocation policy and qualified/template-call spelling. |
| C8-C10 | Result, input, and extra-tensor validation calls. One live public TorchCppABI family; rejected as broader ABI work. |
| **C11** | **`int64_t _known_nnz = Input_values.size(0)`. One live cardinality query, exactly representable by existing `VarInit` and `MemberCall`; selected.** |
| C12-C13 | Adaptive `_nnz` and `_chunk` scheduling state. Live, mutually coupled optimization policy; rejected as unrelated optimization work. |
| C14 | Atomic declaration retained only in unread compatibility state while codegen emits its own declaration. Non-emitting/DCE-like; rejected. |
| C15-C16 | Workspace thread count and aligned-buffer owner. Live allocation pair; rejected as generalized allocation work. |
| C17 | All-COO output-vector `resize`. Constructed only in the grouped tree discarded by the production scalar route; rejected as non-emitting. |
| W1-W5 | Compressed-Where worker view, count/fill `clear`, and compound pool construction. Live DS/DSS ownership family; accurate custom types, direct allocation, and standalone member-call statements remain absent. |
| W6-W9 | Count/offset vectors, prefix loop, fill base, and totals. W3/W9 are individually expressible, but the smallest coherent offset family has two producer templates and remains rooted in raw allocation/prefix construction. |
| W10-W14 | Position, coordinate, and value Torch allocation/pointer pairs plus the position-copy loop. Live compound Torch allocation family; rejected. |
| W15 | Compound result declaration, nested storage assignments, and return. Live result-ABI assembly; rejected as broader ABI/member-lvalue work. |
| D1 | Const/restrict dense pointer from an addressed structured access. Live and compatibility-parsed; const-pointer and exact address spelling remain unresolved. |
| S1/P1 | Relayout and ordinary sparse prefetch conditionals. Live optimization-specific conditional/address representations; rejected. |
| S2/S3 | Direct-initialized heap-tile and packed-operand vectors. Live generalized allocation family; rejected. |
| R1 | Common `RawStmt` detached reconstruction, not a semantic producer; this explains 38 constructors versus 37 producers. |

The nine remaining direct subscript strings were also re-audited and kept
separate from the raw-statement slice:

| Family | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| P1/P2 | Post-op extra-tensor reads occur only under the unsupported untiled workspace fallback; non-emitting in supported production. |
| W1 | Untiled dense-workspace read is bypassed by the dense-result `memcpy`; sparse result levels receive sparse workspaces. |
| C1/C2 | All-COO pre-scan reads are constructed in a grouped tree discarded by the scalar-accumulator production branch. |
| G1/G2 | Group-start reads are discarded with that grouped tree and also require checked vector `.at(...)` semantics. |
| I1/I2 | Root coordinate-position placeholders are replaced by literal zero and `crd_tensor.size(0)` before returned LLIR is built. |

These nine are the unmigrated remainder of the original 22-site subscript
inventory; the other 13 were closed by the preceding narrow structured-access
slices. The remaining ternary is likewise in the discarded all-COO grouped
pre-scan. None of these sites is a coherent live emitted family; migrating them
would be DCE-adjacent cleanup.

C11 was previously rejected only because receiver-call IR did not exist.
`MemberCall` now supplies the exact representation without a new parser,
hierarchy, ABI contract, allocation abstraction, or optimization:

```python
llir.VarInit(
    var=llir.Var("_known_nnz", llir.DataType.INT64),
    value=llir.MemberCall(
        base=llir.Var(
            sparse_values_tensor,
            llir.DataType.TORCH_TENSOR,
        ),
        member="size",
        args=(
            llir.Literal(
                value=0,
                data_type=llir.DataType.INT64,
            ),
        ),
    ),
)
```

It emits byte-for-byte:

```cpp
int64_t _known_nnz = Mask_values.size(0);
```

The target, Torch-tensor receiver, call, tuple, and dimension literal are fresh
compiler-owned nodes. The receiver denotes the existing validated by-value
Torch tensor handle and borrows caller storage without mutation. Independent
lowerings produce disjoint mutable containers and receiver `Var` objects while
retaining structural equality and hashing.

C11 is live when scalar accumulation preserves a sparse output and the ordered
RHS list contains a compressed or coordinate leaf. Default DS-mask -> OO SDDMM
covers the compressed-leaf route; all-COO SDDMM covers the coordinate-leaf
route. The local is emitted before known-size coordinate/value allocation and
is consumed by the existing `ResultTensorAssembler` extent contract.

Construction occurs at the one-shot result/ABI assembly barrier after sparse
prefetch, dense-pointer hoisting, single-iteration elimination, and
loop-invariant factor hoisting. Dynamic-vector rewriting then validates and
detachedly reconstructs the `VarInit`, receiver, member call, and argument in
deterministic order. It has no matching vector declaration and changes no
spelling. Assignment deduplication does not inspect this `VarInit`; the seven
remaining generic rewrites do not consume it. Schedule lowering leaves the
top-level declaration unchanged and common codegen emits it.

Malformed or forged member fields fail closed at the dynamic-vector owner with
the exact four completed pre-assembly pass records. A failure while constructing
the statement belongs to nested `RESULT_ABI_ASSEMBLY`, preserves the original
error object, records no premature ABI success, leaves caches empty, and
suppresses dynamic rewriting, schedule lowering, C++ generation, build-request
assembly, and native loading.

After the slice:

- 379 production `Var` constructors;
- ten direct expression strings: nine subscripts and one ternary;

- 12 known indirect sinks/clones, adding only the accurately typed
  `sparse_values_tensor` receiver;

There is still no direct opaque call, member, initializer, qualified, or
separately classified arithmetic expression in a production `Var.name`, no
`std::move(` in a production `Var.name`, and no string-expression assignment
target.

The exact no-native activation command was:

```sh
PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/src" python - <<'PY'
from collections import Counter
import inspect
from tools import benchmark_compiler_ir as bench
from scorch import ops
from scorch.compiler import llir
from scorch.compiler.scheduler import regblock_force
from scorch.layout import TensorSpec

events = []
sources = []
orig_init = llir.MemberCall.__init__
orig_summary = bench._prepared_source_summary

def traced(self, base, member, template_args=None, args=None):
    orig_init(self, base=base, member=member, template_args=template_args, args=args)
    if (
        member == "size"
        and type(self.base) is llir.Var
        and self.base.type is llir.DataType.TORCH_TENSOR
        and self.base.name.endswith("_values")
        and self.template_args == ()
        and len(self.args) == 1
        and type(self.args[0]) is llir.Literal
        and self.args[0].value == 0
        and self.args[0].data_type is llir.DataType.INT64
    ):
        events.append(inspect.currentframe().f_back.f_code.co_name)

def summary(prepared):
    sources.extend(prepared.request.cpp_sources)
    return orig_summary(prepared)

def invoke_sddmm():
    specs = (
        TensorSpec("oo", (2, 3), name="Mask"),
        TensorSpec("dd", (2, 4), name="Query"),
        TensorSpec("dd", (3, 4), name="Key"),
    )
    with regblock_force(False):
        return ops.einsum(
            "ij,ik,jk->ij", *specs, compile_only=True, format="oo"
        )

llir.MemberCall.__init__ = traced
bench._prepared_source_summary = summary
try:
    cases = [
        *bench._build_latency_cases(),
        bench.LatencyCase(
            "all_coo_positive",
            "ij,ik,jk->ij",
            ("oo", "dd", "dd"),
            "oo",
            invoke_sddmm,
        ),
    ]
    for case in cases:
        events.clear()
        sources.clear()
        _, _, _, runs = bench._time_captured_compilation(case)
        marker = sum(s.count("int64_t _known_nnz = ") for s in sources)
        stage_counts = Counter(r["stage_id"] for r in runs)
        print(
            case.name,
            dict(Counter(events)),
            "source_markers",
            marker,
            "A/L",
            stage_counts["result_abi_assembly"],
            stage_counts["cin_lowering"],
        )
finally:
    llir.MemberCall.__init__ = orig_init
    bench._prepared_source_summary = orig_summary
PY
```
